area.reviews.1.quote: We've relied on City & Suburban Heating & Cooling for years when it came to HVAC repairs on old systems (old home and new) but the current AC/furnace we had was getting very close to the end of its life. After City & Suburban came out to repair our condenser unit this summer, we could have kept sinking money into repairs but we didn't want to be forced into an…
area.reviews.2.quote: Rob has taken great care of our HVAC systems for several years. During his most recent seasonal service it became clear it was the right time to replace the almost 20-year-old AC units. Rob put together a reasonable estimate using top of the line equipment. The install crew was friendly, professional and showed up on time. They get full marks for hauling the equipment up five flights of stairs to…
area.reviews.3.quote: When another company purported that I needed to replace my central air conditioning unit, I called Rob from City and Suburban for a second opinion. He quickly diagnosed the problem as a minor leak that could be repaired quickly, and he restored the unit to life at a fraction of the cost that I would have otherwise paid. The air conditioner continued to operate for years, by the way.
area.reviews.4.quote: Our furnace broke yesterday. We had appts with multiple companies and the one that came out first gave us a quote on a broken part. We almost went with them, but the appt window they offered for the repair would have been too long to wait. The next appt we had was with Rob from City & Suburban Heating & Cooling.
area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in an older house, a large new one and a shop
area.scope.1.why: Older Winnetka houses often still heat with a boiler and radiators; newer ones run furnaces.
area.scope.2.why: Large houses can run a furnace and AC for each floor or wing, so a repair starts with finding which one has failed.
area.scope.3.why: Radiator-heated houses have no ducts for central air, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits.
area.scope.4.why: In houses by architects like Maher, Griffin and Van Bergen, new equipment has to be placed with care inside and out.
area.scope.5.why: Shops in Hubbard Woods and on Elm Street run rooftop units or small furnaces, so opening hours set the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.faq.heading: Winnetka HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Is the boiler in my older Winnetka house worth repairing, or does it need replacing?
area.faq.2.q: Do you come out to Winnetka from Chicago?
area.faq.3.q: Can you cool an older Winnetka house without ductwork?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC work in Winnetka need a permit?
area.faq.1.a: Often it's worth repairing. We diagnose first, and where the boiler has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.cta.body: Have the make of your boiler, furnace or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In a larger house, tell us which floor or wing has the problem.

extras.faq.2.a: Yes. Winnetka is on our service area list, about 13 miles north of the shop at 1225 N Cleaver St, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Usually, yes. Radiator-heated houses have no ducts for central air, so cooling means ductless mini-splits, placed to suit the house.
extras.faq.4.a: Installing or replacing a furnace or air conditioning does: the Village of Winnetka asks for the equipment's specs and where it goes. A repair or tune-up is a different job. Ask whoever quotes an install who pulls the permit.

permits.source: No permit graph: City of Chicago building permits (ydr8-5enu) stop at the city limits, and the Village of Winnetka doesn't publish its permits as open data.
permits.village_data: Village of Winnetka: a permit is required to install or replace building equipment, furnaces and air conditioning included (Building Permits page); the furnace checklist asks for a building permit application, a trade-specific work form, the manufacturer's specifications and the unit's location (Furnace Permit PDF, rev. 2019). No open permit dataset found (searched 15 Oct 2026). City & Suburban: 0 in the Chicago file, all years.
